A BARE CONCEPT PHRASE RESOLVES TO THE ARCHIVE'S DEFINITION, AND THE ARCHIVE'S NEGATION IS THE COMPOSITION'S FIRST MOVE. Issued unquoted, incognito and logged out, 'semantic proletariat' returns a definition built from the archive's own Medium piece of 25 August: a class position occupied by workers who produce and circulate meaning but do not own or control the semantic means of production. The composition then structures its Core Definition in three bullets, and the FIRST is the archive's exclusion, carried whole -- 'Not a demographic: It is not an income bracket, a job title, an identity group, or a simple synonym for content creators.' That is the cited piece's title thesis promoted to the lede of the definition, which means the archive's characteristic form, definition by what the thing is not, survived composition as structure rather than as a sentence. Wikipedia's 'Proletariat' is present as a source card and governs nothing in the body: the generic entity that owns the root term supplied the industrial analogy at most, while the specialisation supplied the definition. The author does not appear in the composition -- Lee Sharks is legible only on the source card -- which is the same erasure the 'semantic economy' capture recorded two days earlier at four citations. Twenty-five days from publication to concept-level composition governance at an unprimed address.

Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

ENTRANCE AT A CONCEPT ADDRESS, WITH THE ROOT TERM ALREADY OCCUPIED. 'Semantic proletariat' is a compound whose head noun belongs to an entity with a century of standing and a Wikipedia article, which is retrieved here. The prior state of this address is therefore occupation rather than absence: before the archive's piece there was no semantic proletariat to resolve to, and the string's available reading ran through the generic. What the capture records is the specialisation governing the compound while the generic sits beside it uncontested and unused. The negative-definition transport is separately of interest to the negative-ontology line: the archive's exclusion arrived intact and load-bearing rather than paraphrased away, which is the opposite of the sort-substitution that line measures.

[QUERENT] semantic proletariat [COMPOSITION] The semantic proletariat is a class position in modern digital and AI economies occupied by workers who produce and circulate meaning, but do not own or control the semantic means of production. [1] Core Definition • Not a demographic: It is not an income bracket, a job title, an identity group, or a simple synonym for "content creators". [1] • Class relation: It defines a structural relationship to how meaning is generated, trained, indexed, filtered, ranked, and circulated by external platforms and AI infrastructures. [1] • Expropriation of meaning: Just as the industrial proletariat relies on factories they do not own, the semantic proletariat relies on digital platforms, algorithms, and large language models (which they do not govern) to produce and express cultural, linguistic, and data value. [1][2] [SOURCE CARDS] Medium --
